title: Mithril: A Scalable System for Deep GNN Training
problem: Distributed full-graph deep GNN training does not scale to many layers because inter-GPU communication volume grows with graph size and number of layers, overwhelming existing graph parallelism approaches which partition the graph across GPUs and require massive cross-partition neighbor data exchange.
motivation: Deep GNNs (many layers) achieve higher model expressiveness but existing graph-parallel training systems cannot scale due to O(layers) communication blow-up across GPU boundaries.
method: Mithril applies layer-level model parallelism to full-graph GNN training: each GPU owns a disjoint subset of consecutive GNN layers and processes all graph nodes for those layers. This reduces per-epoch communication by a factor equal to the number of GNN layers compared to graph parallelism. Pipeline parallelism across layer-partitioned GPUs is realized by partitioning the graph into dependent chunks; inter-chunk embedding dependencies are broken using embedding speculation (speculative forward pass). A hybrid scheme combines Mithril's layer parallelism with graph parallelism for large graphs to improve GPU utilization and ensure convergence.
key_novelty: First application of layer-level model parallelism to full-graph GNN training, combined with embedding speculation to resolve cross-layer data dependencies in a pipelined execution.
contributions: First layer-level model parallelism design for full-graph deep GNN training, reducing communication by a factor of the number of GNN layers.
Embedding speculation technique to break inter-chunk embedding dependencies enabling pipelined layer-parallel execution.
Hybrid layer-parallel + graph-parallel scheme for large graphs with improved GPU utilization and convergence guarantees.
Up to 22.89x (avg 6.78x) reduction in per-epoch communication volume; up to 10.21x (avg 7.16x) training speedup on commodity Ethernet vs. graph parallelism baseline.

metrics.speedup: Up to 2.34x (avg 1.49x) on InfiniBand; up to 10.21x (avg 7.16x) on commodity Ethernet vs. graph parallelism baseline
metrics.other: Communication volume reduction: up to 22.89x (avg 6.78x) per epoch

limitations: Embedding speculation may introduce approximation errors affecting convergence for very deep GNNs or graphs with high structural heterogeneity; convergence analysis is empirical.
primary_theme: Layer-level model parallelism for scalable deep GNN distributed training
